packet.headline_seed: Iran demands guarantees for World Cup participation
packet.description_seed: The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) has presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup in the US, Mexico and Canada.

what: Iran demands guarantees for World Cup participation

clean_source_blocks.text: Iran has indicated it will take part in this summer's football World Cup, but has demanded a series of guarantees from Fifa and the tournament's hosts amid growing tensions surrounding the team's participation. The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) said Iran would compete at the tournament "without any retreat from our beliefs, culture and convictions", while insisting the hosts "must take our concerns into account". The demands come after FFIRI president Mehdi Taj was denied entry to Canada before last month's Fifa Congress. Taj later revealed Iran had presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup, which begins on 11 June in the United States, Mexico and Canada.
The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) has presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup in the US, Mexico and Canada.

The Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran (FFIRI) has thrown the 2026 World Cup into the spotlight by issuing a strict 10-point ultimatum to the host nations. Despite qualifying for the tournament, Tehran has warned that their participation depends on specific security and visa guarantees following recent diplomatic friction. The FFIRI has officially stated that while the men’s national team intends to compete in the 2026 World Cup, they will only do so if the joint hosts - the United States, Mexico and Canada - meet a set of stringent conditions. This follows a period of intense geopolitical tension and a regional conflict that has cast a shadow over the tournament's build-up.

Among the demands published in a statement on Saturday are guarantees that all players, coaches and officials travelling with the team will receive visas, including those who completed military service with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The group is listed as a terrorist organisation in Canada and the US, and Mehdi Taj's links to it were cited as a reason he was denied entry into Canada. Iran is also seeking assurances over the treatment of the national team, including respect for the Iranian flag and national anthem, as well as enhanced security at airports, hotels and stadiums during the tournament. Some of the requests are likely to prove easier for Fifa to influence than others. Fifa can help oversee tournament logistics, official protocols and the treatment of participating delegations during the competition itself.

[Lähde: BBC World]
Iran has indicated it will take part in this summer's football World Cup, but has demanded a series of guarantees from Fifa and the tournament's hosts amid growing tensions surrounding the team's participation.

The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) said Iran would compete at the tournament "without any retreat from our beliefs, culture and convictions", while insisting the hosts "must take our concerns into account".

The demands come after FFIRI president Mehdi Taj was denied entry to Canada before last month's Fifa Congress.

Taj later revealed Iran had presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup, which begins on 11 June in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

Among the demands published in a statement on Saturday are guarantees that all players, coaches and officials travelling with the team will receive visas, including those who completed military service with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The group is listed as a terrorist organisation in Canada and the US, and Mehdi Taj's links to it were cited as a reason he was denied entry into Canada.

Iran is also seeking assurances over the treatment of the national team, including respect for the Iranian flag and national anthem, as well as enhanced security at airports, hotels and stadiums during the tournament.

Some of the requests are likely to prove easier for Fifa to influence than others.

Fifa can help oversee tournament logistics, official protocols and the treatment of participating delegations during the competition itself.

But questions involving visas, border controls and security vetting ultimately remain under US jurisdiction rather than Fifa regulations.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has already stated that Iranian footballers would be welcome at the tournament, while warning that individuals with links to the IRGC could still face restrictions on entering the United States.

That leaves Fifa facing a delicate balancing act between ensuring the participation of all qualified teams and navigating the political realities surrounding relations between Tehran and Washington.

[Lähde: USA TODAY]
Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) president Mehdi Taj has demanded assurances from FIFA that his country's military won't be insulted in the United States during the World Cup.

Iranian soccer officials are set to meet with FIFA regarding their participation in the tournament, which runs from June 11 to July 19 in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Iran's status for the World Cup has been up in the air since the U.S. and Israel launched an armed conflict against the Middle East nation in late February.

Taj was denied entry to Canada for last week's FIFA Congress due to his previous service in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), an elite branch of Iran's military.

The IRGC is considered a terrorist organization in both the U.S. and Canada.

Addressing the FIFA Congress in Vancouver, FIFA president Gianni Infantino made it clear that he expected Iran to be present at the competition in North America.

But according to Taj, the threat of another incident like the one in Canada last week could imperil Iran's participation in the World Cup.

"We need a guarantee there, for our trip, that they have no right to insult the symbols of our system – especially the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps," Taj told Iranian state broadcaster IRIB on Tuesday, May 5.

"This is something they must pay serious attention to. If there is such a ​guarantee and the responsibility is clearly assumed, then an incident like what happened in Canada will not happen again."

Last week, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran is welcome this summer, but added that the U.S. may bar anyone in the traveling delegation with ties to the IRGC.

"They can’t bring a bunch of IRGC terrorists into our country and pretend that they are journalists and athletic trainers," Rubio said.

According to Taj, without assurances that Iran's traveling delegation will be allowed into the U.S. and not insulted, it may not be able to participate in the World Cup.

payload.title: Iran vaatii takeita MM-kisoihin osallistumiselle
payload.summary: Iranin jalkapalloliitto on esittänyt Fifalle ja vuoden 2026 MM-kisojen isäntämaille kymmenen ehtoa, jotka koskevat muun muassa viisumeita, turvallisuutta sekä maajoukkueen kohtelua turnauksen aikana.
payload.content:
Iranin jalkapalloliitto FFIRI ilmoittaa maan aikovan osallistua vuoden 2026 jalkapallon MM-turnaukseen, mutta vaatii Fifalta ja kisojen isäntämailta selkeitä takeita ennen turnausta. Vaatimukset koskevat erityisesti viisumeita, turvallisuusjärjestelyjä sekä sitä, miten Iranin maajoukkuetta, lippua ja kansallislaulua kohdellaan Yhdysvalloissa, Meksikossa ja Kanadassa pelattavissa kisoissa.

## Kymmenen ehtoa Fifalle ja isäntämaille

Iran on esittänyt Fifalle kymmenen ehtoa osallistumiselleen. Liiton mukaan miesten maajoukkue aikoo kilpailla turnauksessa, mutta ei tingi omista arvoistaan, kulttuuristaan tai näkemyksistään. Samalla FFIRI on korostanut, että isäntämaiden on otettava Iranin huolenaiheet huomioon.

MM-turnaus alkaa 11. kesäkuuta, ja sen järjestävät yhdessä Yhdysvallat, Meksiko ja Kanada. Iranin vaatimukset ovat nousseet esiin tilanteessa, jossa joukkueen osallistumisen ympärillä on kuvattu olevan kasvavia jännitteitä. Taustalla on myös FFIRI:n puheenjohtajaa Mehdi Tajia koskenut tapaus: häneltä evättiin pääsy Kanadaan ennen Fifan kongressia.

## Viisumit ja turvallisuus keskiössä

Keskeinen osa Iranin vaatimuksista liittyy maahantulolupiin. FFIRI haluaa takeet siitä, että kaikki joukkueen mukana matkustavat pelaajat, valmentajat ja toimihenkilöt saavat viisumit. Vaatimus koskee myös henkilöitä, jotka ovat suorittaneet asepalveluksen Iranin vallankumouskaartissa. Vallankumouskaarti on luokiteltu terroristijärjestöksi Kanadassa ja Yhdysvalloissa, ja Tajin yhteydet siihen mainittiin syynä hänen Kanadaan pääsynsä epäämiselle.

Iran hakee lisäksi vakuutuksia maajoukkueen kohtelusta turnauksen aikana. Esillä ovat Iranin lipun ja kansallislaulun kunnioittaminen sekä vahvistetut turvatoimet lentoasemilla, hotelleissa ja stadioneilla. Vaatimukset liittyvät sekä joukkueen käytännön matkustamiseen että sen asemaan virallisissa kisajärjestelyissä.

## Fifan vaikutusvalta on rajallinen

Kaikki Iranin esittämät vaatimukset eivät ole Fifan suoraan päätettävissä. Järjestö voi vaikuttaa turnauksen logistiikkaan, virallisiin protokolliin ja osallistuvien delegaatioiden kohteluun kilpailun aikana. Sen sijaan osa viisumeihin ja maahantuloon liittyvistä kysymyksistä riippuu isäntämaiden omista viranomaispäätöksistä.

Iranin ilmoitus lisää poliittista painetta MM-kisojen valmisteluihin. Maa on kuitenkin viestinyt, että sen maajoukkue aikoo pelata turnauksessa, jos osallistumisen käytännön edellytyksistä, turvallisuudesta ja virallisesta kohtelusta saadaan sitä tyydyttävät takeet.

Iran has indicated it will take part in this summer's football World Cup, but has demanded a series of guarantees from Fifa and the tournament's hosts amid growing tensions surrounding the team's participation. The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) said Iran would compete at the tournament "without any retreat from our beliefs, culture and convictions", while insisting the hosts "must take our concerns into account". The demands come after FFIRI president Mehdi Taj was denied entry to Canada before last month's Fifa Congress. Taj later revealed Iran had presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup, which begins on 11 June in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) has presented Fifa with 10 conditions for participation at the World Cup in the US, Mexico and Canada.

The Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran (FFIRI) has thrown the 2026 World Cup into the spotlight by issuing a strict 10-point ultimatum to the host nations. Despite qualifying for the tournament, Tehran has warned that their participation depends on specific security and visa guarantees following recent diplomatic friction. The FFIRI has officially stated that while the men’s national team intends to compete in the 2026 World Cup, they will only do so if the joint hosts - the United States, Mexico and Canada - meet a set of stringent conditions. This follows a period of intense geopolitical tension and a regional conflict that has cast a shadow over the tournament's build-up.

Among the demands published in a statement on Saturday are guarantees that all players, coaches and officials travelling with the team will receive visas, including those who completed military service with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The group is listed as a terrorist organisation in Canada and the US, and Mehdi Taj's links to it were cited as a reason he was denied entry into Canada. Iran is also seeking assurances over the treatment of the national team, including respect for the Iranian flag and national anthem, as well as enhanced security at airports, hotels and stadiums during the tournament. Some of the requests are likely to prove easier for Fifa to influence than others. Fifa can help oversee tournament logistics, official protocols and the treatment of participating delegations during the competition itself.
